# ProductLockup

Combines an Adobe app icon, a product label, and an optional caret into a single reusable identity unit — the building block for global nav, cards, and product tiles.

  - Alternatives: link-card: A card that is one link: illustration or icon, a headline, optional description, an arrow affordance. The whole surface is the target and the headline is the accessible name.; card: A non-interactive content card; actions live in a slot.; collection: A row, grid or scroller of one repeated unit.; button: Triggers an action. A label, optional leading and trailing icons, and the full interactive state set.; checkbox / radio: A selection control with a checked state, usually paired with a label.; toggle / switch: A binary on/off control that applies immediately.; input / field: Accepts typed input. Label, value, placeholder, and an error state.; badge / tag / chip: A small label. Non-interactive unless it is dismissible.; pagination: Moves between pages of content.; accordion: A disclosure: a trigger that shows and hides a region of content. Open or closed is a prop a consumer sets, not an interaction state.; select / dropdown: A choice among options. The native <select> does the choosing; the design styles the trigger around it.; helper text: Guidance or a message under a field: hint, error, success. Associated with its field, never floating.; list: A sequence of like items — features, links, steps. The items are the content; the list is the rhythm.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: —

- The Label is the accessible name — keep it as real text (not an image) so screen readers announce the product. WCAG 1.1.1 / 4.1.2.
- Decorative app icons: if the Label already names the product, mark the app icon aria-hidden so it isn't announced twice. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
- When the lockup is a link or nav item, make the whole unit one focusable target with a clear name — not separate tab stops for icon and text. WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose.
- Contrast, especially knockout / inverse on media: keep the label and icons at 4.5:1 (text) / 3:1 (UI) against the surface; add a scrim on imagery. WCAG 1.4.3 / 1.4.11.
- Order: the app icon precedes the label in the DOM so it reads in a logical sequence. WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.
